acceptance: A forge-cli test scaffolds all four dialects and asserts each tree carries .forge-interpret; it fails on the three non-Rust dialects before the fix (new.rs:491-493 gates the marker on Lang::Rust).
forge-control-plane interp.rs module doc no longer says the interpreted route runs behind the server-build gate (main line 14 does today).

On the dev stack (forge-platform-operations/dev/up-full.sh), a Python workspace made by forge new --dialect python and pushed with forge push converges and its op answers through the edge; the scripted repro and its output are in the step evidence.
author: rory

gaps.note: Diffed the IP-2 step acceptance and the plan intent (blocker 2: non-Rust dialects push and never converge) against the recorded intent statement and the tree: new.rs:491-493 writes .forge-interpret only for Lang::Rust; forge-control-plane main interp.rs:14 still says the route runs behind the server-build gate. All three acceptance bullets map one-to-one onto recorded acceptance; nothing in the intent is left uncovered.

gaps.description: Plan (brief forge-cli--step-ip2/.harness/briefs/IP-2.md) diffed against the intent statement: the step lands in two repos but the run had only a forge-cli lane, so the interp.rs doc fix had nowhere to land; opened forge-control-plane--step-ip2 and named both lanes in the brief.
Brief also asks for a sweep of forge-cli docs/templates for other text claiming only Rust trees get the marker, beyond the intent statement
gaps.note: the README already promises push-serves for every dialect, and a stale claim elsewhere would re-mislead the same customer the fix is for; it is a grep, not scope creep.

gaps.description: Implementer repro showed the marked Python tree converges on the CP but the runtime refuses the app-less bundle (validate_app_bundle requires app_manifest, which the CP omits since R-8 a818087); the intent "served on its first push" is unmet without it, so the step now lands in forge-runtime too (lane forge-runtime--step-ip2, brief IP-2b-runtime.md).

statement: A workspace scaffolded by forge new --dialect in any of Python, TypeScript, Java or Rust carries the .forge-interpret marker, so its first git push takes the interpreted reconcile route and converges with no operator action; forge-control-plane src/git/reconcile/interp.rs module doc describes the route as it is (no server-build gate, FORGE_GIT_INTERPRET kill switch only).
